- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% to capture reversal bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 78–80), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force a 2–3 day mean-reversion correction toward prior 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early (first 5–7 days) and underestimates late (last 5–7 days); apply asymmetric smoothing: reduce early peaks, amplify late troughs.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” (neutral) followed by positive, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of momentum to forecast.
- When sentiment is uniformly positive for 3+ consecutive days, model overestimates by 5–10%; apply a 5–10% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 3 days, model is likely misaligned with sentiment; re-calibrate using sentiment-weighted moving average of last 5 days.
